limitations: Repository-only: this packet adds three new research modules (pure-stdlib Ed25519 verify, pinned public-key trust store, v3 signing envelope validator/verifier), an EMPTY committed operational trust store, value-blind test fixtures, one stdlib test, three governance docs (ADR-0124, migration/admission analysis, runbook) and a new evidence manifest, and wires the test into the Makefile governance target and the CI governance job. NOTHING is deployed. No key is generated, held, pinned, rotated or revoked; no private key is in the repository, tests, argv, logs, fixtures or Notion; no NAS mount / SMB auth / producer-host / broker / MT5 contact; no dataset read; no release is built, signed, published or consumed.

The operational verification path is DARK by default: the committed trust store is empty, so any ed25519-v1 envelope fails closed (unknown_signing_key) until a real producer public key is pinned out-of-band under a separate Sponsor GO (GO #2a). No real/operational key or algorithm selection is performed here.

The test fixtures were produced offline by an EPHEMERAL Ed25519 test key; the private seed was created in memory and NEVER written, printed or persisted. Only the public key, its fingerprint and the resulting (public) signatures are committed. Regeneration requires a producer-side signer (out of scope for TIM, which verifies only), mirroring production reality.

Documented limitation (RULE 5): created_at_utc is bound into the signed material (signing time is tamper-evident) but the key_validity window OBJECT is not; the authoritative validity decision is trust-store membership + active status + the pinned window checked against the signed created_at_utc. Stated in ADR-0124 and the migration doc rather than implied.

The producer GuvFXData / GUVFX_DATA_ROOT readiness (Blocker 2) is UNVERIFIABLE from this checkout and remains BLOCKED; it is NOT claimed as verified. The migration/admission doc records only the verification contract (scripts/check_data_root.py) the producer must satisfy, and the first-release admission checklist marks every item beyond the repository contract as a separate Sponsor-gated step not performed here.

Handoff docs (STATUS/HANDOFF/NEXT/KNOWN_ISSUES) were intentionally NOT edited to avoid conflicts with concurrent sessions; the handoff is carried by this manifest, ADR-0124, the migration/admission analysis, the runbook, and the TIM Notion master record.

reviewer: Author self-review + an independent adversarial security review (differential fuzz of the Ed25519 verifier against the cryptography/OpenSSL oracle over ~90k verify comparisons + mutation testing of the 50-test suite; trace of every algorithm/flag path for downgrade/relabel/replay/trust-store-bypass; boundary + value-blindness audit). Verdict: PR-READY, NO CRITICAL and NO HIGH exploitable against a legitimately pinned full-order key; the operational path is dark (empty store). Four hardening items were FIXED before PR-ready and re-verified by a fresh differential fuzz (400 genuine signatures accepted, 0 over-acceptances across 5400 adversarial cases, small-order keys now rejected): (MEDIUM-1) the verifier was non-strict (accepted non-canonical / small-order points the oracle rejects, exploitable only if a low-order key were pinned) -> _decodepoint now rejects non-canonical y>=p and a set sign bit on x==0, and ed25519_verify rejects small-order A/R; (MEDIUM-2) the malleability-guard test passed for the wrong reason (S==L on the RFC vector is rejected by the core equation anyway) -> added a genuine-signature (R, S+L) twin test that fails if the S<L guard is removed; (MEDIUM-3) require_operational defaulted False so a forgeable synthetic envelope could be accepted by a careless operational caller -> added verify_operational_release_signature_v3 which hard-codes require_operational=True and a mandatory trust store; (LOW-6) the trust store could pin a low-order key -> _validate_entry now refuses a non-canonical/small-order Ed25519 key via is_acceptable_public_key. LOW-4 (K-7 cross-bind runs only when manifest= supplied) and LOW-5 (signed_manifest_path not bound into the signed material) are documented as deliberate defence-in-depth-only items in ADR-0124 and the migration doc rather than changed, since the manifest digest + release id are the authoritative binding. Boundary clean: only new files added; the byte-frozen contracts.py/tim_contracts.py/tim_fixtures.py and tim_contracts_v0_3.py are unchanged; no signing/keygen primitive and no network/host/NAS/broker import.
